# Cedric Stanhope

## Overview

- **Age:** Sixteen years old  <sub>[v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)</sub>
- **Origin:** Boston, United States  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>
- **Role:** Poet  <sub>[v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Yankee  <sub>[v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>; Uncle Cedric  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>

## Appearance

In his earlier youth, Cedric had delicate features, a small face with crimson lips, and dark blue eyes framed by chestnut curls. As he reached sixteen, he grew into an impressive six-foot tall man with short-cut brown hair.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)_

## Personality

Cedric is a thoughtful, polite, and imaginative boy with a brilliant mind and strong sense of fairness. He possesses great manliness, excelling in games and maintaining his own ground despite his delicate outward appearance. He is deeply appreciative of nature and poetry, turning his rich inner world of fancies into written verse.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c7 P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), [v2 c8 P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c23 P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033)_

## Goals

- Desires to become a six-foot-tall man like his father  <sub>[v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)</sub>

## History

Cedric Stanhope arrived in Brierley from Boston to reside with his grandmother near the shore and attend the school taught by Nell Harcourt. He quickly formed a deep bond with Nell, whom he viewed as a kindred spirit and teacher. As a child, he created imaginary rock companions along the shore and enjoyed books and fairy tales. He brought about the reunion of his father and Rosalind Penrose after telling his father about Miss Rosalind, leading to their eventual marriage. As he matured into his teenage years, he grew rapidly in height, developed a passion for football, and began composing poetry. His poems gained published success, culminating in his initial collection. He attended Nell Harcourt's wedding to Hugh Carrow, driving them to the train station afterward, before making plans to travel abroad for two years of study.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c11 P42](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0042), [v2 c29 P5](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0005), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033), [v4 c4 P16](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0016), [v4 c17 P27](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0027)_

## Background by volume

- Moved from Boston to Brierley to live with his grandmother  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- Had an undecided fight over national flags with St. Clair Trask  <sub>[v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>
- Reserved the title of 'mother' exclusively for his late mother  <sub>[v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>

## Quotes

> I ask you to take these, teacher, which I discovered in the field belonging to Mr. Duckett, and I returned so I could offer them to you since I believed you were a lady who would appreciate them, and also because . . . teacher, I am fond of you.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> I love him most of all in the world, and then Grandma Stanhope, and after that, you, teacher. Were it not my obligation to love Grandma Stanhope next to father on account of everything she is doing for me, I would love you second to him.  <sub>[v2 c15 P9](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0009)</sub>

> Is it not wonderful that we are that type, teacher?  <sub>[v2 c15 P19](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0019)</sub>

> Teacher, you will never age. You belong to those lucky human beings who discovered and imbibed the Fountain of Youth,—you alongside Mother Rosalind. Look at this! After you get married, calling you Mrs. Carrow is something I WILL NOT do. For me, your name will forever be 'Teacher’—the instructor who gave me the finest lessons I was ever taught.  <sub>[v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>
